races.name: Mercedes-Benz Of Chichester Mares' Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Sorgean
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with Harry Fry's excellent 2/3 strike rate suggesting strong preparation after 32-day break

runners_data.name: Hidden Fortune
runners_data.note: Natural front runner whose point-to-point win over 3 miles suggests stamina to see out this trip strongly
runners_data.comment: 3m point winner for whom the step up in trip could be a firm plus on hurdle debut
runners_data.spotlight: Point winner (3m, good to yielding) who was runner-up on both bumpers starts (good to soft/good); she's a sister to a 3m hurdle winner and the step up in trip could be a firm positive on her first hurdle start.

runners_data.name: Secret Des Lune
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter who has led in recent starts but may pay for forcing early fractions

runners_data.name: Queens Up
runners_data.note: Lightly raced hold-up horse whose stamina is unproven at this trip despite recent hurdle experience

runners_data.name: Rock Sensation
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with strongest RPR/TS figures who benefits from 144-day break under Nick Scholfield

runners_data.name: Shutfrontdoor
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid recent form but Moore stable's 0/28 record raises preparation concerns

runners_data.name: Whodunit
runners_data.note: Prominent runner carrying 6lb weight allowance but fading finish tendency makes her vulnerable in traffic

runners_data.name: Diamond White
runners_data.note: Prominent type with consistent placed form who needs clear run to utilize her tactical speed

runners_data.name: Saffron Belle
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with fade-in-finish concerns whose recent form suggests she needs more time

runners_data.name: Flash Bardot
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with solid RPR 113 rating who can benefit if the pace sets up correctly

races.paceDynamic: Secret Des Lune and Hidden Fortune will contest the early lead, with Secret Des Lune's three front-running efforts suggesting she'll force the pace. Hidden Fortune's point-to-point win and two bumper seconds show she can lead strongly, creating a legitimate speed duel. Four horses (Sorgean, Shutfrontdoor, Whodunit, Diamond White) want prominent positions behind them, guaranteeing traffic problems at the business end. This honest gallop followed by congestion 2-3 out will favour hold-up horses who can avoid the scramble and find clear runs late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Speed Duel Benefits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Secret Des Lune and Hidden Fortune go too fast early and burn each other out
scenarios.body: The pace collapse allows hold-up runners to sweep past the weakening leaders and prominent racers caught in traffic. Rock Sensation and Flash Bardot can time their runs perfectly from the back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Hidden Fortune settles better than Secret Des Lune and kicks clear 3 out
scenarios.body: Her point-to-point stamina tells as the pace moderates, allowing her to build an unassailable lead before the closers can respond. The prominent brigade get shuffled back in the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Escape Traffic
scenarios.trigger: If Sorgean or Shutfrontdoor get first run on the leaders before the pack closes
scenarios.body: One prominent runner times their move perfectly to avoid the inevitable squeeze, capitalizing on their tactical position. Harry Fry's 2/3 record suggests Sorgean gets the perfect ride.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders stop quickly and the prominent horses also weaken from the early pace
scenarios.body: The race becomes a staying test where any horse with stamina reserves can win, regardless of early position. Queens Up's longer trip experience could prove decisive despite her light rating.

watchPoints.text: Secret Des Lune and Hidden Fortune could go too fast early, setting up a pace collapse that changes the entire complexion
Sorgean, Shutfrontdoor, Whodunit and Diamond White all wanting prominent positions creates inevitable traffic problems 2-3 out
Rock Sensation returning after 144 days could need the run despite her superior ratings on paper
Freddie Mitchell's 3lb claim on Shutfrontdoor helps offset the Moore stable's poor recent form
Queens Up is unproven at this trip but her light weight suggests connections expect improvement

races.name: KSR Lighting Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Belgarum
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 168 days off with first-time cheekpieces, needs to prove fitness but has strong course form

runners_data.name: Sun Joy
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent performer with good recent form, well-handicapped and should appreciate the likely pace scenario

runners_data.name: Motazzen
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who can dictate terms, recent winner but carries 7lbs penalty for that success

runners_data.name: Oakley
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits this tactical setup, recent winner in good form but amateur jockey Mr Stone adds uncertainty

runners_data.name: Bel Ombre
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who needs a strong pace to be effective, fitted with first-time hood and tongue-tie for focus

runners_data.name: Taritino
runners_data.note: Another hold-up horse requiring genuine tempo, well-treated on handicap mark but needs things to fall right

runners_data.name: Hiconic
runners_data.note: Returning after 256 days absence with first-time tongue-tie, prominent style could work if retaining ability

runners_data.name: Khalk'eau Spigao
runners_data.note: Inexperienced hold-up horse carrying light weight, needs significant pace improvement to be competitive

races.paceDynamic: Motazzen will take the field along at a steady clip from the front, with Belgarum, Sun Joy, Oakley and Hiconic content to track in behind. The lack of genuine pace pressure means Motazzen can dictate terms without being harried early, creating a tactical advantage for the leader. Hold-up horses Bel Ombre, Taritino and Khalk'eau Spigao will need the race to develop into a strong gallop to be competitive. This tactical setup clearly favours prominent runners and the leader, as they can position handy without expending energy fighting for position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Motazzen Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Motazzen is allowed to dictate a comfortable pace unchallenged
scenarios.body: The leader gets an easy time of it and kicks clear turning for home before the hold-up horses can mount their challenge. Prominent runners like Oakley and Sun Joy benefit from the strong position but may struggle to peg back the leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Battle Develops
scenarios.trigger: If Sun Joy or Oakley apply early pressure to Motazzen
scenarios.body: The increased tempo plays into the hands of those tracking the pace, with fresher legs available for the finish. This creates opportunities for the better-rated prominent runners to strike.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Challenge Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely strong throughout and hold-up horses get room
scenarios.body: Bel Ombre and Taritino can use their closing kick to maximum effect in a truly-run race. The front-runners tire and become sitting ducks for the swooping finishers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Upset Materializes
scenarios.trigger: If the favourites fail to handle the track conditions or jumping
scenarios.body: Khalk'eau Spigao's light weight or Hiconic's return to form creates an opening for an outsider. The race falls apart tactically allowing an unfancied runner to capitalize.

watchPoints.text: If Motazzen gets an uncontested lead, he becomes very difficult to peg back given his ability to control the race
Sun Joy and Oakley must not get into an early battle for position, as this would compromise their finishing kick
Hold-up horses Bel Ombre and Taritino need other pace angles to emerge or they'll have too much ground to make up
Amateur jockey Mr Stone on Oakley requires monitoring for tactical positioning and whether he can deliver at the right moment
First-time headgear on Belgarum and Hiconic suggests connections seeking improvement after disappointing recent efforts

races.name: Fontwell Park Half Year Membership Novices' Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: All Authorized
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning to fences after 38 days off for in-form Moore yard, needs strong pace to be effective

runners_data.name: Ballyfinn
runners_data.note: Prominent racer carrying 7lb penalty after Wednesday's Fontwell win but unexposed over fences and suited by tactics
runners_data.comment: Breakthrough win here (3m2f) last Wednesday; down in trip under 7lb penalty; key candidate
runners_data.spotlight: Made the breakthrough on his fifth start over fences when scoring here (3m2f, good) last Wednesday; back down in trip under 7lb penalty but not fully exposed and looks a key player.

runners_data.name: Lord Maher
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits but major concern over 161-day absence despite retaining ability on ratings

runners_data.name: Thickthorn Tom
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for powerful Skelton stable adding tongue-tie to cheekpieces, unexposed but needs pace collapse
runners_data.comment: Second chase start when third (3m) latest; tongue-tie added and unexposed for top yard
runners_data.spotlight: Much the best of two chase starts when third of 11 at Exeter (3m, good to soft) in March; drops back in trip with a tongue-tie joining his cheekpieces; unexposed and he's respected for top yard.

runners_data.name: Jaffa Cake
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner likely to get easy lead, poor recent form but tactical advantage significant

runners_data.name: Lunar Ocean
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who makes mistakes, pulled up last time but has shown consistency when completing
runners_data.comment: Mainly consistent over fences; excuses last time and not ruled out in first-time blinkers
runners_data.spotlight: Can make mistakes but mainly consistent over fences for this yard; pulled up at Warwick after an error last time but 2m and ground that was likely faster than good were probably not ideal; that brought his record to 0-18 but he's not ruled out in first-time blinkers back up in trip.

runners_data.name: Misteroddsocks
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in good recent form but carrying concerns over ability to handle this longer trip

races.paceDynamic: Jaffa Cake will take this field along from the front, with Ballyfinn, Lord Maher, and Misteroddsocks likely to track him in the prominent positions early. With only one confirmed front runner and several prominent racers, the pace should be genuinely run but not suicidal, allowing the early leaders to dictate terms. The three hold-up horses (All Authorized, Thickthorn Tom, Lunar Ocean) will need the pace to collapse or find significant improvement to overcome their tactical disadvantage. This race shape strongly favours horses that can race prominently and have something left for the finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Jaffa Cake sets a reasonable pace and the prominent horses can follow the tempo
scenarios.body: The race becomes a test of stamina between the front group, with hold-up horses struggling to make up ground on good ground over this trip. Ballyfinn's recent winning form and Lord Maher's class give them the edge over the sustained pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Jaffa Cake gets an easy lead and the field allows him too much rope early
scenarios.body: The leader builds an unassailable advantage jumping the last few fences, with his stamina proving decisive over this extended trip. The prominent horses fail to close the gap despite their superior ratings.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Challenge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes too strong and the front runners weaken significantly
scenarios.body: The race falls apart from the second last fence, allowing one of the hold-up horses to capitalize on superior class or fitness. Thickthorn Tom's Skelton yard form and All Authorized's higher grade experience become crucial factors.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If Jaffa Cake goes too slow early and it becomes a sprint from the home turn
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace turns this into a tactical affair where superior class and finishing kick matter most. The better-rated horses can unleash their turn of foot despite racing from behind.

watchPoints.text: Jaffa Cake getting too easy a lead early - if unopposed through the first mile he could steal a march on superior rivals
Lord Maher's jumping after 161 days off - any early mistakes could ruin his prominent racing style
Lunar Ocean's jumping errors - has history of costly mistakes that could end his chances despite fitness
Thickthorn Tom's headgear changes - tongue-tie addition suggests connections seeking improvement
Ballyfinn carrying his penalty - watch if the 7lb rise affects his ability to keep up with early pace

runners_data.name: Hurst Hill

runners_data.name: Jager Time

runners_data.spotlight: Safely held in first two handicaps (2m3f/3m, good to soft) and absent since January but remains unexposed (particularly on good ground) and is worth a glance in the betting.

runners_data.name: Counteract
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up horse who gets in light at the weights but lacks recent competitive form

runners_data.name: Nelson Gate
runners_data.note: Young hold-up horse from an out-of-form yard but has shown ability in similar contests

runners_data.name: Porridge
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner in poor recent form who needs significant improvement to feature

runners_data.name: For Old Times Sake
runners_data.note: Sole pace-setter wearing new tongue-tie but has a tendency to fade in the finish
runners_data.comment: Struggled in last two handicaps and now 0-6 over hurdles but not written off just yet
runners_data.spotlight: 0-6 over hurdles, having struggled in his last two handicaps (2m4f/2mf, good; warm favourite on first occasion); goes up in trip fitted with new tongue-tie; has a lot to prove but can't be written off yet.

runners_data.name: Gone Country
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse prone to late fading who faces a difficult task from his patient style

runners_data.name: Anothermanicmonday
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner switching to left-handed track after jumping left, but needs significant improvement
runners_data.comment: Beaten about 60l on recent handicap debut at Exeter (2m2f); up in trip here
runners_data.spotlight: Jumped left throughout and was beaten about 60l on recent handicap debut at Exeter (2m2f, good); this switch to a left-handed track is an obvious move but he needs to take a big step forward over the new trip.

races.paceDynamic: For Old Times Sake is the sole confirmed front runner and will dictate terms from flag to flag without early pressure. The prominent runners Renoir, Lady Henrietta and Tell The Tale will track the leader through the early stages, while the bulk of the field including Hurst Hill, Jager Time, Nelson Gate and Porridge will sit patiently off the pace. With most runners preferring to come from behind and For Old Times Sake prone to fading late, this sets up a sustained gallop that will suit the hold-up horses who can produce their finishing kicks in the final half-mile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If For Old Times Sake maintains a steady gallop without burning out early
scenarios.body: The patient trackers get the perfect setup to unleash their finishing speed up the Fontwell hill. The lack of early pace pressure allows the hold-up specialists to position perfectly and strike when it matters.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent horses can get close enough to For Old Times Sake without being strung out
scenarios.body: Renoir or Lady Henrietta can use their forward positions to pounce when the leader weakens, avoiding the traffic problems that could hinder the back markers. Their tactical positioning proves crucial in a race where timing matters.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leader Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If For Old Times Sake handles the extended trip better than expected and doesn't fade late
scenarios.body: The new tongue-tie helps For Old Times Sake maintain his gallop to the line, with the hold-up horses leaving their runs too late on the testing Fontwell finish. Harry Cobden's experience proves vital in managing the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If For Old Times Sake stops quickly or falls, leaving no clear pace-setter
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy tactical affair with the prominent runners forced to go forward earlier than ideal, suiting those with the most natural speed. The lack of a true pace test changes the complexion completely.

watchPoints.text: For Old Times Sake's early pace will determine the entire race shape - if he goes too fast early he'll stop quickly
Watch the positioning of Hurst Hill and Jager Time turning for home as they need clear runs to unleash their finishing kicks
Monitor how aggressively the prominent runners Renoir and Lady Henrietta track the leader through the early stages
Nelson Gate's positioning will be crucial given the Moore yard's poor recent form affecting confidence
Observe if Tell The Tale shows any rustiness early after his 117-day absence from competition

races.name: V2 Radio Handicap Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Gone In Sixty
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with strong recent form but needs pace to aim at, which may be lacking here

runners_data.name: Ballywood
runners_data.note: Front runner who gets ideal scenario with uncontested lead, though 12-year-old legs are a concern

runners_data.name: Grain Trade
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with highest rating but trainer struggling and relies on others for pace

runners_data.name: Holy Legend
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse carrying bottom weight but poor recent form and needs strong gallop

runners_data.name: Daany
runners_data.note: Prominent runner freshest of all with just 9 days since last run and good recent second

runners_data.name: Saint Polo
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with solid recent form but sharp drop back in trip from 3m to 2m2f is questionable
runners_data.comment: Unexposed in h'cap hurdles and back down in trip for this chase debut; cheekpieces added
runners_data.spotlight: Went close on handicap debut over hurdles at Sedgefield (2m4f) in March before solid third at Taunton (3m, also good) one month later; drops sharply back in trip with cheekpieces enlisted and he remains unexposed on this introduction to fences.

runners_data.name: Millies Mite
runners_data.note: Prominent runner but poor recent form with three consecutive pulled-ups is major concern

runners_data.name: Model Approach
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse and recent winner but inexperienced 5-year-old stepping up in class significantly

races.paceDynamic: Ballywood is the sole confirmed pace-setter and will face no early pressure, allowing him to dictate a sustainable gallop from the front. With prominent runners Daany and Millies Mite likely settling just behind, and the majority of the field (Gone In Sixty, Grain Trade, Holy Legend, Saint Polo, Model Approach) adopting hold-up tactics, this creates a classic scenario where the pace-setter gets an easy lead. The lack of pace pressure means Ballywood can conserve energy for the finish, while the large contingent of hold-up horses will be relying on each other for late pace. This race shape strongly favours front-running and prominent tactics over hold-up horses who may find insufficient pace to run at.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Ballywood gets the uncontested lead he's likely to receive
scenarios.body: The 12-year-old can control the tempo completely and kick clear when the jumps thin out the field behind him. With most rivals needing to come from off the pace, he can exploit their reliance on each other for a strong gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up brigade can generate enough pace among themselves despite the lack of early speed
scenarios.body: Gone In Sixty's class advantage and strong recent form could tell, while Grain Trade's higher rating might prove decisive if pace materializes. The winner emerges from a late cavalry charge of closers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Daany or Millies Mite can track Ballywood and outstay him
scenarios.body: The prominent horses get the perfect trip behind the lone leader and have enough tactical speed to respond when Ballywood comes under pressure. Recent winner Model Approach could also benefit from this scenario if positioned closer than usual.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If Ballywood goes too slowly and the race becomes a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The lack of any pace pressure creates a tactical mess where positioning and jumping become crucial factors. Saint Polo's higher rating could prove telling in a slowly-run affair where class rises to the top.

watchPoints.text: Ballywood getting a soft lead could prove decisive given the lack of pace pressure he'll face
Gone In Sixty needs others to go fast enough early to set up his finishing kick
Model Approach moving closer to the pace than usual would suggest connections fancy their chances
Millies Mite's recent habit of pulling up makes him a potential non-finisher
Saint Polo's ability to handle the sharp drop back in trip from his recent 3m efforts

races.name: Best Of British Events Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Red One
runners_data.comment: Represents a top stable and is closely related to two useful jumpers; shortlisted
runners_data.spotlight: Sixth foal; closely related to useful winners Guard Your Dreams (2m-2m4f hurdle/chase) and Carys' Commodity (2m3f-2m6f hurdle/chase); dam unraced half-sister to useful bumper/jumps winner The Jigsaw Man; with a top stable; must be considered.

runners_data.name: Norff N Sauff
runners_data.comment: Half-brother to fair hurdler/chaser Quick Sharpener; stable does pretty well in bumpers
runners_data.spotlight: 24,000euros 3yo; seventh foal; half-brother to fair hurdler/chaser Quick Sharpener and a point winner; dam unraced half-sister to hurdle/chase winner Off The Charts; stable does pretty well in bumpers.
